_schema._description: Chorus interludes keyed by chapter label. Shown the first time a student enters that chapter, above the scene narrative.

Capitulum I.latin: heu, Thebae miserae! pestis crescit. dei tacent. cur fata sic dura sunt? rex, audi populum tuum.
Capitulum I.en: Alas, wretched Thebes! The plague grows. The gods are silent. Why are the fates so harsh? O king, hear your people.

Capitulum II.latin: rex veritatem investigat. sed veritas in tenebris dormit. cave, rex — quod quaeris, te vulnerabit.
Capitulum II.en: The king searches for truth. But truth sleeps in darkness. Beware, O king — what you seek will wound you.

Capitulum III.latin: vates caecus quod oculi non vident videt. heu, rex superbe! ira veritatem non mutat.
Capitulum III.en: The blind seer sees what the eyes cannot. Alas, proud king — anger does not change the truth.

Capitulum IV.latin: regina antiqua oracula timet. heu, memoria! quod sepultum est, surgit.
Capitulum IV.en: The queen fears the old oracles. Alas, memory! What is buried rises again.

Capitulum V.latin: nuntius ex Corintho venit. nova videntur bona — sed dolor sub gaudio latet.
Capitulum V.en: A messenger comes from Corinth. The news seems good — but sorrow lurks beneath the joy.

Capitulum VI.latin: pastor antiquus tandem locutus est. omnia nota sunt. silentium nunc plenum est.
Capitulum VI.en: The old shepherd has spoken at last. All is known. The silence is now heavy.

Capitulum VII.latin: rex se ipsum iudicat. quale fatum eligit? fortes quattuor portae stant.
Capitulum VII.en: The king judges himself. What fate will he choose? Four gates stand before him.

Capitulum VIII.latin: fabula completa est. fata cunctos vincunt. sed homo electionem habet.
Capitulum VIII.en: The story is complete. The fates conquer all — yet a human keeps his choice.

Prologus.latin: in via ad Thebas, monstrum exspectat. iuvenis, audi: aenigma vita aut mors est.
Prologus.en: On the road to Thebes, a monster waits. Young man, listen — this riddle is life or death.
